items.pronunciation_notes: The -ों is a hummed o, not a separate syllable: skuu-loṁ, two beats, then the nasal में behind it.
items.gloss_en: Class 2 plural oblique on a borrowed noun

learn.explanation_en: Class 2 is defined by its ending, not its origin. स्कूल, बाज़ार, स्टेशन and होटल all came into Hindi from other languages, and because none of them ends in -ा they behave exactly like घर: unchanged in the singular, -ों in the plural. That is worth saying plainly, because learners often assume foreign-looking words are exceptions. They are not — the ending decides everything in this module.

examples.note: Plural before a postposition, so -ों appears.
Same ending on a Persian-origin word.

examples.english: There are children in the schools.
examples.note: बच्चे is the subject, so it stays direct — only स्कूलों sits before में.

common_error.why_en: -ें is a feminine plural ending. A masculine plural before a postposition takes -ों, whatever the noun's origin.

practice.prompt_en: More than one school. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: स्कूल + में
practice.explanation_en: Plural before a postposition, so the ending is -ों. The unchanged form स्कूल में would mean one school.

game.explanation_en: स्कूलें में uses a feminine plural ending on a masculine noun. It should be स्कूलों में.

items.pronunciation_notes: दिनों has the hum on the second syllable, then तक is short and flat: di-noṁ tak.

learn.title_en: Time words split across two classes
learn.explanation_en: दिन and साल do not end in -ा, so they are Class 2 and never change in the singular. महीना and हफ़्ता do end in -ा, so they are Class 1 and become महीने and हफ़्ते. In the plural the two classes converge — महीनों, हफ़्तों, दिनों, सालों all take the same -ों — so the only place the distinction bites is the singular. Time phrases are where you will meet this constantly, because तक and से attach to them all day long.

examples.note: Plural oblique with तक.
The same ending with a different postposition.
A number in front does not change what the noun has to do.

common_error.why_en: दिन is masculine, so its plural before a postposition is दिनों. दिनें is not a form Hindi has.

practice.prompt_en: More than one year. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: साल + से
practice.explanation_en: Plural before से, so साल becomes सालों.

game.explanation_en: दिनें is a feminine-shaped plural on a masculine noun. दिनों तक is correct.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first o is long and open, the second is the nasal hum: lo-goṁ ko.
items.gloss_en: a noun that is already plural in meaning

learn.title_en: लोग is plural before you touch it
learn.explanation_en: लोग means people, and it is plural in meaning already — there is no singular लोग meaning one person, which is what आदमी is for. Because it is plural, it takes the plural oblique ending whenever a postposition follows: लोगों को, लोगों से, लोगों के साथ. This one is worth drilling on its own, because लोग को is an error English speakers make for months, translating the unmarked English word people straight across.

examples.note: Plural in meaning, so plural in form.
के साथ counts as a postposition, so the -ों is required.

examples.english: There are people in the village.
examples.note: Here लोग is the subject, so it stays direct — only गाँव is oblique.

common_error.why_en: लोग is already plural, and a plural noun before a postposition must carry -ों.

practice.prompt_en: Put this noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: लोग + को
practice.explanation_en: लोग is plural, so before को it becomes लोगों.

game.explanation_en: लोग is plural and sits before के साथ, so it must be लोगों के साथ.

summary.recap_en: Class 2 is finished. Any masculine noun that does not end in -ा is unchanged in the singular and takes -ों in the plural — including borrowed words, time words, and लोग, which is plural before you touch it.
summary.next_up_en: Next: Class 3, the masculine nouns that end in -ी. They look as though they should change, and in the singular they do not.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with the long ii at the end: aad-mii ko. The middle vowel is barely there in speech.
items.gloss_en: Class 3 singular — no change at all

learn.title_en: The class that looks like it should move
learn.explanation_en: आदमी is masculine, which surprises learners because it ends in -ी and -ी usually signals feminine. You met that warning back in Module 4. What matters here is that the -े ending belongs to Class 1 alone: it is what a final -ा turns into. आदमी has no -ा to convert, so in the singular it does nothing at all before a postposition. आदमे is not a word.

examples.note: Identical to the direct form.
A different postposition, the same non-event.
No postposition here, so nothing would change anyway.

common_error.why_en: -े is what a final -ा becomes. आदमी ends in -ी, so there is nothing for that ending to attach to.

practice.prompt_en: One man. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: आदमी + से
practice.explanation_en: One man, and Class 3 nouns are unchanged in the singular, so आदमी stays as it is.

game.explanation_en: आदमे को applies the Class 1 ending to a noun that has no final -ा. The form is आदमी को.

items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy bh, then two vowels running together into one long glide: bhaa-ii se.

learn.explanation_en: भाई is written with the full vowel ई rather than the matra ी, but for the purposes of this module that is a spelling difference and nothing more. It is masculine, it does not end in -ा, and so it sits in Class 3 and stays exactly as it is in the singular. The spelling difference does start to matter in the plural, which is the next level — and it is where most of the errors on this word live.

examples.note: Unchanged before से.
Unchanged before को as well.
भाई is the subject and stays direct; only घर stands before a postposition.

common_error.why_en: The -े ending exists only for Class 1 nouns ending in -ा. भाई does not qualify.

practice.prompt_en: One brother. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: भाई + को
practice.explanation_en: One brother, so the singular form is used, and Class 3 singulars do not change. भाइयों को is the plural.

game.explanation_en: भाए is not a Hindi word. भाई does not change in the singular oblique.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ह is a light breath between the two vowels, not a hard sound: da-hii meṁ.
items.gloss_en: Class 3 mass nouns, which have no plural

learn.title_en: The ones that never go plural
learn.explanation_en: दही, पानी and घी are the masculine -ी nouns Module 4 asked you to memorise with their gender, because nothing about them predicts it. They are also mass nouns — you do not count them — so the plural question never arises for them at all. That makes them the easiest members of Class 3: unchanged in the singular, and there is no second form to learn.

examples.note: The -ी stays exactly as it is.
Same class, same non-event.

examples.english: There is water in the house.
examples.note: पानी is the subject here, so it is direct — only घर sits before the postposition.

common_error.why_en: पानी ends in -ी, not -ा, so the Class 1 ending never applies to it.

practice.prompt_en: Put this noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: पानी + में
practice.explanation_en: पानी is a Class 3 mass noun. It is unchanged, and पानियों is not a form the word has.

game.explanation_en: पाने में converts a -ी ending as though it were -ा. पानी does not change.

summary.recap_en: Class 3 is every masculine noun ending in -ी or -ई. In the singular it does nothing at all, because the -े ending belongs only to nouns with a final -ा. Mass nouns like पानी and दही never go plural, so for them that is the whole rule.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the plural, which is the one place Class 3 does move — and the spelling that almost every learner gets wrong.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four syllables, and the ii of आदमी shortens to a quick i: aad-mi-yoṁ ko.
items.gloss_en: Class 3 plural — the -ी shortens and य appears

learn.explanation_en: In the plural oblique, a final -ी cannot simply carry -ों on its back. Hindi shortens the long ी to a short ि and slides a य in to bridge the two vowels: आदमी becomes आदमियों. The -ों at the end is the same ending you have seen since Class 1 — it has not changed, only what happens in front of it has. Say the word out loud and the reason becomes obvious: aad-mi-yoṁ flows, aad-mii-oṁ does not.

examples.note: Long ी shortens, य bridges, -ों closes.
The noun's form does not depend on which postposition follows.
A number makes the plural explicit but does not do the work for you.

common_error.why_en: The long ी cannot take -ों directly. It shortens to ि and a य appears between the vowels.

practice.prompt_en: More than one man. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: आदमी + को
practice.explanation_en: Plural oblique of a -ी masculine: shorten the vowel, add य, then -ों.

game.explanation_en: आदमीों keeps the long vowel and stacks -ों on it. The correct plural is आदमियों.

items.pronunciation_notes: The long ii of भाई shortens here: bhaa-i-yoṁ, three syllables before के लिए.
items.gloss_en: Class 3 plural where the vowel is written full

learn.explanation_en: भाई becomes भाइयों, and the change is easier to see here than with आदमी because the vowel is written as a full letter: ई shrinks to इ, and य appears. Learners almost universally write भाईयों, keeping the long vowel and adding the ending on top. That spelling is wrong, and it is wrong for the same reason आदमीों is — Hindi will not stack -ों on a long vowel.

examples.note: के लिए is a postposition, so the plural must be oblique.
Same form, different postposition.
The shortest of the three, and the one you will use most.

common_error.why_en: The long ई shortens to इ before the य. Keeping it long is the single most common misspelling of this word.

practice.prompt_en: More than one brother. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: भाई + के लिए
practice.explanation_en: Short इ, then य, then -ों. Every other option either keeps the long vowel or drops the य.

game.explanation_en: भाईयों keeps the long ई. The plural oblique is भाइयों.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated th, then the shortened vowel: haa-thi-yoṁ ko.
items.gloss_en: the pattern generalised to any -ी masculine

learn.explanation_en: Once the shape is visible it applies everywhere, and the meaning of the noun is irrelevant: हाथी becomes हाथियों just as आदमी becomes आदमियों. This is worth noticing because it is the first point in the module where you can predict a form for a word nobody has taught you. If it is masculine and it ends in -ी, the singular does nothing and the plural is -ियों. Two facts cover the whole class.

examples.note: Singular, so unchanged.
Plural, so shortened vowel plus य plus -ों.
The postposition changes; the noun does not.

common_error.why_en: Same trap as भाईयों — the long vowel must shorten before the य.

practice.prompt_en: More than one elephant. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: हाथी + को
practice.explanation_en: हाथियों. Note that हाथों is a real word, but it is the plural oblique of हाथ, meaning hands.

game.explanation_en: हाथीयों keeps the long ी. The plural oblique is हाथियों.

summary.recap_en: Class 3 has exactly one moving part: in the plural the long final vowel shortens and a य appears before -ों. आदमी to आदमियों, भाई to भाइयों, हाथी to हाथियों. Keeping the vowel long is the error to watch for.
summary.next_up_en: Next: Class 4, the feminine nouns ending in -ी — and a class you can already half predict.

items.gloss_en: Class 4 singular — no change at all
items.pronunciation_notes: The ड़ is a flap, tongue struck once against the roof of the mouth: laṛ-kii ko.

learn.title_en: Feminine -ी: nothing happens in the singular
learn.explanation_en: लड़की is feminine and ends in -ी, and before a postposition it does not change: लड़की को. Here is the honest version of what Class 4 is. In its forms it behaves exactly like Class 3 — unchanged in the singular, -ियों in the plural. It gets a class of its own because of gender, which decides adjective agreement and का or की, both coming later in this module. So the forms are a free ride; the gender is the thing to hold on to.

examples.note: Identical to the direct form.
Unchanged again.
लड़की is the subject and stays direct; स्कूल is the one sitting before में.

common_error.why_en: लड़के is the oblique of लड़का, which is a different word meaning boy. लड़की does not change at all.

practice.prompt_en: One girl. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: लड़की + से
practice.explanation_en: One girl and no change in the singular, so लड़की से. लड़के belongs to लड़का, and लड़कियों is the plural.

game.explanation_en: लड़का is Class 1 and must become लड़के before a postposition. The direct form cannot stand there.

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex ट with the tongue curled back, then the long ii: be-ṭii se.
items.gloss_en: Class 4, and the cleanest contrast pair in Hindi

learn.title_en: बेटा and बेटी, side by side
learn.explanation_en: बेटा and बेटी are the same word with two endings, and they land in different classes because of them. बेटा is Class 1 and becomes बेटे before a postposition; बेटी is Class 4 and becomes nothing at all. Holding this pair in mind is the fastest way to keep the two classes apart, because the meaning is identical and the ending is doing all the work. If you can produce बेटे को and बेटी को without hesitating, Class 1 and Class 4 are secure.

examples.note: No change before से.
No change before को either.

examples.hindi: बेटा और बेटी घर में हैं।
examples.read_as: beṭaa aur beṭii ghar meṁ haiṁ.
examples.english: My son and daughter are at home.
examples.note: Both are subjects, so both stay direct — only घर is oblique.

common_error.why_en: बेटे is the oblique of बेटा. If you mean the daughter, the form is बेटी, unchanged.

practice.prompt_en: One daughter. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: बेटी + से
practice.explanation_en: बेटी is Class 4 and unchanged in the singular. बेटे belongs to बेटा, and बेटा से is not possible at all before a postposition.

game.explanation_en: बेटा ends in -ा, so it cannot stand in its direct form before से. It must be बेटे से.

tts_strings: बेटा और बेटी घर में हैं।

items.pronunciation_notes: The double ल is held slightly longer than a single one, which is what separates बिल्ली from बिली: bil-lii ko.

learn.explanation_en: बिल्ली behaves like every other Class 4 noun, and it gives a good chance to see को doing something other than marking an object. In बिल्ली को दूध पसंद है the को marks who the liking belongs to — Hindi says the milk is pleasing to the cat. You met this shape in Module 5 with आपको. What matters here is that को is still a postposition, so the noun in front of it still has to be oblique, whatever job the को is doing.

examples.note: Unchanged, like every Class 4 singular.
को marks the one who likes; the form of बिल्ली is unaffected by that.

examples.english: The cat is in the house.
examples.note: Here बिल्ली is the subject, so it is direct — and it looks the same either way.

common_error.why_en: बिल्ला is a separate masculine word for a tomcat. If you mean बिल्ली, it does not change.

practice.prompt_en: One cat. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: बिल्ली + को
practice.explanation_en: Class 4 singulars do not change, so बिल्ली को.

game.explanation_en: बिल्ले is the oblique of the masculine बिल्ला. For बिल्ली the form stays बिल्ली को.

summary.recap_en: Class 4 is the feminine -ी nouns, and in the singular they change no more than Class 3 does. The pair बेटा and बेटी shows why the class exists: the ending decides the class, and the class decides what has to happen before a postposition.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the Class 4 plural, and the single most misspelled form in beginner Hindi.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four beats with the vowel shortened in the middle: laṛ-ki-yoṁ ko.
items.gloss_en: Class 4 plural — shorten, bridge with य, add -ों

learn.title_en: The form worth getting right the first time
learn.explanation_en: लड़की becomes लड़कियों, by exactly the process you learnt for आदमी two levels ago: the long ी shortens to ि, a य bridges the vowels, and -ों closes the word. लड़कीों is not a rare mistake or a regional spelling — it is simply not a possible Hindi word, because the script and the sound system both refuse it. Notice what this means: Class 3 and Class 4 produce identical plural shapes. The gender difference is invisible here and shows up only once adjectives and का or की arrive.

examples.note: The full change: shorten, bridge, close.
के साथ is a postposition, so the plural must be oblique.
Same dative को as with बिल्ली, now on a plural.

common_error.why_en: A long ी cannot carry -ों directly. It shortens to ि and takes a य before the ending.

practice.prompt_en: More than one girl. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: लड़की + को
practice.explanation_en: लड़कियों को. The other three each keep a vowel that has to change or borrow an ending from another class.

game.explanation_en: लड़कीों stacks -ों onto a long ी. The form is लड़कियों.

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex ट, then the shortened vowel and the hum: be-ṭi-yoṁ ke lie.
items.gloss_en: Class 4 plural, and where the two -ी classes meet

learn.explanation_en: बेटी becomes बेटियों, and if you compare it with भाइयों from level eight the two are built identically. This is the useful summary of the last four levels: every noun ending in -ी, masculine or feminine, makes its plural oblique the same way. You do not have to know the gender to produce the form. You will have to know it very soon — बेटियों के लिए and बेटों के लिए take different adjectives and different possessives — but not for this.

examples.note: Plural oblique before के लिए.
The same form with a shorter postposition.

examples.hindi: यह किताब बेटियों के लिए है।
examples.read_as: yah kitaab beṭiyoṁ ke lie hai.
examples.english: This book is for the daughters.
examples.note: किताब is the subject and stays direct; बेटियों is the word standing before के लिए.

common_error.why_en: The long ी shortens to ि before the य. This is the same trap as भाईयों and हाथीयों.

practice.prompt_en: More than one daughter. Put the noun into its oblique form.
practice.question: बेटी + को
practice.explanation_en: बेटियों को — shorten the vowel, add य, then -ों.

game.explanation_en: बेटीयों keeps the long ी. The plural oblique is बेटियों.

tts_strings: यह किताब बेटियों के लिए है।

items.pronunciation_notes: साथ has an aspirated th and a long aa; the phrase runs as laṛ-ki-yoṁ ke saath.
items.gloss_en: direct and oblique plurals side by side in speech

learn.title_en: लड़कियाँ and लड़कियों in the same conversation
learn.explanation_en: This exchange puts the two plurals next to each other so the difference is audible rather than theoretical. लड़कियाँ is the direct plural — it is what you use when the girls are the subject and nothing follows them. लड़कियों is the oblique plural, and it only appears because के साथ is standing behind it. Listen for the ending: the direct form hums on aaṁ, the oblique on oṁ. That one vowel is carrying the whole grammatical difference.

lines.speaker: A
lines.hindi: क्या तुम भी लड़कियों के साथ हो?
lines.read_as: kyaa tum bhii laṛkiyoṁ ke saath ho?
lines.english: Are you with the girls too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: हाँ, मैं लड़कियों के साथ हूँ।
lines.read_as: haaṁ, maiṁ laṛkiyoṁ ke saath huuṁ.
lines.english: Yes, I am with the girls.

common_error.why_en: लड़कियाँ is the direct plural and cannot stand before a postposition. के साथ forces the oblique लड़कियों.

practice.question: मैं ___ के साथ हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: के साथ is a postposition and the meaning is plural, so the oblique plural लड़कियों is required.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: The speaker says लड़कियों — the oblique plural, because के साथ follows it.

tts_strings: क्या तुम भी लड़कियों के साथ हो?
हाँ, मैं लड़कियों के साथ हूँ।

summary.recap_en: Class 4 plurals are built exactly like Class 3 plurals: लड़की to लड़कियों, बेटी to बेटियों. लड़कीों does not exist. The dialogue puts लड़कियाँ and लड़कियों side by side, where the only audible difference is the final vowel — and that vowel is the entire grammar.
summary.next_up_en: Next: Class 5, the feminine nouns that do not end in -ी — किताब, रात, बात — where the plural takes plain -ों instead.
